S050-01.notes: Small trial and short duration are reasons for caution, i.e. not to overstate. Dismiss conflicts with 'promising'; replicate/conceal do not fit the cited limitations.

S050-02.notes: Sentence 2 sets up the contrast with the later outcry. D is the main trap but the text shows people did object; A is too literal; C is unsupported.

S050-03.notes: Inhibitor leached only by heavy rain, so seeds sprout only when there is enough moisture. B contradicts; C/D are unsupported. Factually sound: rain-gauge germination inhibitors that leach from seed coats are documented in desert annuals.

S050-04.notes: 30k/50k=60%, 30k/120k=25%; the arithmetic is right. C is the only choice that addresses both parts of the claim (equal absolute gain, different percentages).

S050-05.notes: A comma closes the nonrestrictive 'which' clause before the main verb 'has'. B leaves the clause open; a semicolon or dash cannot pair with the opening comma.

S050-06.notes: Singular subject 'tradition' with an intervening clause; 'continues'. A/C are plural; B is a nonfinite verb.

S050-07.notes: The later surveys show it was evidently true that early explorers saw only the entrance. Consequently reverses the cause (seeing only the entrance caused the modest description, not the other way round). Similarly and Nonetheless do not fit the logic.

S050-08.notes: The goal requires both the finding (slower regrowth with age) and context for an unfamiliar audience. A states the finding without saying what an axolotl is, so it is the strong trap. B/D omit the finding.

S050-09.notes: 800x0.20=160 and 200x0.30=60; the arithmetic is correct. Only A gives both the count comparison and the percentage contrast. B and C each cover one group; D gives totals.

S050-10.notes: Only D states a similarity. Facts check out: the Amazon is first and the Congo second in discharge; lengths of about 6,400 and 4,700 km are standard; the Congo is the deepest river (over 220 m).
